entities.name: Samut
entities.description: A fast, rash and curious girl of the Tah crop, Djeru and Nakht's friend, who later discovers that the God-Pharaoh is the Great Trespasser.

entities.name: Djeru
entities.description: A cautious, rule-abiding boy of the Tah crop, friend of Samut and Nakht, who finds a hole in the Hekma.

entities.name: Nakht
entities.description: A young aven boy of the Tah crop who can command water and who is killed by a shadowy horror in the desert.

entities.name: Nicol Bolas
entities.description: The God-Pharaoh of Amonkhet, whom Samut learns is a trespasser from elsewhere who caused the calamity rather than saving the plane.

entities.name: Hazoret
entities.description: A god of Amonkhet depicted in an old mural in a different style, and whose temple stands in Naktamun.

entities.name: Oketra
entities.description: A god of Amonkhet who walks among the children and teaches discipline.

entities.name: Kefnet
entities.description: The god of knowledge, whose statue stands in a fountain and who demands inquisitive minds.

entities.name: Rhonas
entities.description: A god of Amonkhet who watches the children train.

entities.name: Bontu
entities.description: A god of Amonkhet whose monument holds a sealed chamber that she has forgotten.

entities.name: Vizier Heqet
entities.description: A vizier who teaches the children and yells at them.

entities.name: Vizier Ahmose
entities.description: A vizier whose words about the Harvest Samut quotes.

entities.name: Setha
entities.description: A child of the Tah crop.

entities.name: Besetha
entities.description: A child of the Tah crop.

entities.name: The Shadowy Horror
entities.description: A towering shadowy monster with a mask-like bone face and a glowing rhombus eye that withers Nakht in the desert.

entities.name: The Risen Dissenters
entities.description: Rotting corpses that rise from an oasis and sands and attack the children, said to be dissenters returned by the curse of wandering.

entities.name: Tah crop
entities.description: The crop of initiates that Samut, Djeru and Nakht are assigned to at their Harvest.

entities.name: Naktamun
entities.description: The great city of Amonkhet, protected by the Hekma.

entities.name: The Hekma
entities.description: A shimmering barrier of water magic that protects Naktamun from the desert wastes.

entities.name: The Luxa
entities.description: The river that flows by Naktamun.

entities.name: Children's Quarters
entities.description: The sleeping quarters where the children are watched over by anointed caretakers.

entities.name: Bontu's Monument
entities.description: A pyramid holding a sealed chamber where Samut finds the God-Pharaoh's true title.

entities.name: The Desert Wastes
entities.description: The desert outside the Hekma where ruins, a half-buried statue, a shrine and monsters are found.

entities.name: Amonkhet
entities.description: The desert plane ruled by the God-Pharaoh.

events.summary: On the eve of their Harvest, Samut finds Nakht by the river and the friends play-fight, joined by Djeru.
events.quote: Samut gave him a playful shove, sending him stumbling back into the water

events.summary: Nakht confesses his fears that the three will be separated and that his faith may falter; Samut says that questions are part of faith.
The trio sneaks out of the Children's Quarters at night, and Nakht reveals he can command water.
events.quote: a small gush of water swirled sprang from the fountain and danced around his fingertips.

events.summary: Samut leads her friends to an old mural of Hazoret and strange fighting forms, which she performs.
events.quote: Samut assumed the first stance on the mural

events.summary: Nakht wonders aloud whether there was a time before the gods, unsettling his friends.
events.quote: if there ever was a time before the gods.

events.summary: Djeru shows his secret, a hole in the Hekma, and Nakht persuades the others to go out and look for themselves.
events.quote: working his way through the near-invisible hole in the Hekma

events.summary: The three children crawl through the barrier into the desert wastes.
events.quote: then dropped to her belly and began crawling through to the other side.

events.summary: In the desert they find a half-buried statue and ruins, and a gigantic limbed thing in the distance sends them fleeing.
events.quote: a looming . . . thing shuffled across the sand.

events.summary: In a ruined shrine they find the word Trespasser freshly carved beneath the God-Pharaoh's symbol.
Rotting corpses rise from the oasis and swarm the shrine, which Djeru calls dissenters returned by the curse of wandering.
events.quote: From the stagnant water and the surrounding sands, rotting corpses started to rise.

events.summary: Nakht draws the risen away and conjures a whirlpool to hold them while Samut and Djeru escape.
events.quote: The stagnant waters beneath him swirled into a whirlpool

events.summary: A shadowy horror freezes Nakht in flight, appears before him, and consumes him.
Samut sees Nakht wither to a lifeless husk, and Djeru tackles her out of sight; they flee back to the city at dawn.
events.quote: She heard his soul-rending screech as he instantly withered and decayed

events.summary: Years later, the loss hardens Djeru's faith while Samut takes up doubt and searches the ancient parts of Naktamun.
events.quote: took up the mantle of doubt and questions

events.summary: Samut finds a sealed chamber in Bontu's Monument and sees the God-Pharaoh named Trespasser.
events.quote: The walls of the shadowed chamber spoke of the God-Pharaoh's first arrival on Amonkhet

events.summary: Samut realizes that the God-Pharaoh is the Great Trespasser who caused the calamity rather than saving the plane, and resolves to warn everyone.
As Samut sprints from the chamber, dark magic flickers to life across the runes.
events.quote: a dark magic slowly flickered to life across the runes.

relations.quote: I think we are good together.
Someone has to keep you two out of trouble.
We are Djeru, Nakht, and Samut of the Tah crop!

relations.note: its touch withers him to a husk
relations.quote: as the shadowy horror touched her friend.

relations.note: protects the city from the desert wastes
relations.quote: a wall powerful enough to stop the sand and shadows that stalked the wastes.

relations.note: she concludes he is the Great Trespasser who caused the calamity
relations.quote: The God-Pharaoh is the Great Trespasser.
